subject: 5-Bullet Friday — The Best Career Advice I’ve Received, A New Group for Parents, Fixing Common Pull-Up Mistakes, and More

bullets.section: Short story I’m reading yet again
bullets.title: They’re Made Out of Meat
bullets.creator: Terry Bisson
bullets.note: . Terry originally made his mark in the science-fiction community with his short story [_Bears Discover Fire_](https://www.amazon.com/Bears-Discover-Fire-Other-Stories/dp/0312890354), which won the Hugo, Nebula, and Locus awards. _They’re Made Out of Meat_, a short story you can read in minutes, has quite a fan base on the Internet and has been adapted for audio, video, and film. You can hear it performed on _This American Life_ [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5usXhX0zaO4).

bullets.title: Sriram Krishnan - The Man Leading America’s AI Race Against China
bullets.note:
on _The Shawn Ryan Show_ ([Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/238-sriram-krishnan-senior-white-house-policy-advisor/id1492492083?i=1000727849030), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/6PPscTResgN3cWLEYOWPvt), [YouTube](https://youtu.be/tar79r-h_4I?si=6rK4WKe3zbe-WWAT)).  
​  
The portion that I want to highlight has nothing to do with AI. It has to do with how Sriram proved himself very early in his career when no one knew him. [Click here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=4319s&v=tar79r-h_4I) to be taken to a great story of Sriram moving to Seattle and impressing one of the all-time best coders at Microsoft. What he did mirrors a lot of what I did after college (in totally different domains) following mentors’ advice, and the strategy still works like gangbusters.  
​  
The clip is only 4–12 minutes long, depending on how far you go, but the gist is this: Niche down until you are THE expert in something very narrow, and you can often do this by combining two things that are rarely combined.

bullets.title: Pmarca Guide to Career Planning Part 2: Skills and education
bullets.note:
Long ago, [Marc Andreessen](https://tim.blog/2016/05/29/marc-andreessen/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit), famed technologist and billionaire investor, had a blog with amazing advice. Then he took the whole thing down. The link in this bullet is a pirated copy of one of his essays from 2007, and there is a lot that overlaps with Sriram’s advice. I’ve basically built my career on some version of this, and it can apply to anyone—a new college student, someone mid-career seeking reinvention, and much more:  
​  
“**Seek to be a double/triple/quadruple threat.  
​  
​**Scott Adams—the creator of Dilbert—[nails it](https://web.archive.org/web/20190202130611/https://dilbertblog.typepad.com/the_dilbert_blog/2007/07/career-advice.html):  
​  
​_If you want an average successful life, it doesn’t take much planning. Just stay out of trouble, go to school, and apply for jobs you might like. But if you want something extraordinary, you have two paths:_

1.  _Become the best at one specific thing._
2.  _Become very good (top 25%) at two or more things._

_The first strategy is difficult to the point of near impossibility. Few people will ever play in the NBA or make a platinum album. I don’t recommend anyone even try.  
​  
The second strategy is fairly easy. Everyone has at least a few areas in which they could be in the top 25% with some effort. In my case, I can draw better than most people, but I’m hardly an artist. And I’m not any funnier than the average standup comedian who never makes it big, but I’m funnier than most people. The magic is that few people can draw well and write jokes. It’s the combination of the two that makes what I do so rare. And when you add in my business background, suddenly I had a topic that few cartoonists could hope to understand without living it.  
​  
...Get a degree in business on top of your engineering degree, law degree, medical degree, science degree, or whatever. Suddenly you’re in charge, or maybe you’re starting your own company using your combined knowledge.  
​_​  
…  
​  
\[Back to Marc\] "The fact is, this is even the secret formula to becoming a CEO. All successful CEOs are like this. They are almost never the best product visionaries, or the best salespeople, or the best marketing people, or the best finance people, or even the best managers, but they are top 25% in some set of those skills, and then all of a sudden they’re qualified to actually run something important.”

bullets.section: What I’m urging friends in London to see
bullets.title: Personality: The Lloyd Price Musical in Concert
bullets.note:
If you don’t know Lloyd Price, his story will blow your mind. [_Personality: The Lloyd Price Musical_](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/whats-on/personality-the-lloyd-price-musical-in-concert/) is playing in London on Saturday, October 11th. [Click here](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/whats-on/personality-the-lloyd-price-musical-in-concert/) to learn more and buy tickets.  
​  
Lloyd’s story is that of beating unbelievable odds. In the span of one year, Lloyd went from digging septic tanks in Louisiana to becoming the first teenager ever to sell more than a million records. ​Lloyd’s innovations went beyond performing music. He also promoted the legendary “Thrilla in Manila” and “Rumble in the Jungle” with Muhammad Ali. Price had the foresight to retain ownership of the copyrights and future royalties of his music, and he was the first artist to start his own record label.
